text:
- chief complaint: left shoulder pain for about three weeks, with no recalled specific injury.
- history of present illness: the patient reports constant left shoulder pain that worsens with pressure and lying on the affected side at night. Pain limits reaching and lifting, and overhead movement is avoided. The patient is active and has been doing heavy basement renovation work. Prior occasional aches were managed with Tylenol. Pain is partially relieved by Tylenol.
- physical examination: limited active and passive range of motion of the left shoulder, with pain on movement. Tenderness over the greater tuberosity of the humerus. No tenderness at the sternoclavicular or acromioclavicular joints. Good hand grip. Capillary refill under 3 seconds and intact light-touch sensation in the left arm. Shoulder X-ray shows no fracture. Vitals reviewed and normal.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: constant left shoulder pain, pain with lifting or reaching, pain with overhead movement, pain with lying on the shoulder. No numbness or tingling.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A. The patient is continuing extra-strength Tylenol two tablets every six to eight hours.
- follow-up instructions: MRI of the left shoulder ordered. Physical therapy referral for six to eight weeks, with educational materials from the nurse. Continue Tylenol. A steroid injection will be considered if symptoms do not improve. Follow-up visit to be scheduled after physical therapy.
